description.text: Opilio Rossi was born on 14 May 1910 in New York to Angelo Rossi and Davidina Ciappa. After his family relocated to Italy during his childhood, he studied at the Collegio Alberoni in Piacenza and earned a doctorate in canon law from the Pontifical Roman Athenaeum “S. Apollinare” in Rome, where his thesis focused on St. Basil. He was ordained a priest on 11 March 1933 and entered the diplomatic service of the Holy See, serving first as an attaché at the Secretariat of State and later as secretary of the nunciatures in Belgium, the Netherlands, and Germany during the turbulent years of the Second World War.

In 1953 he was appointed titular archbishop of Ancyra and nuncio to Ecuador, before moving to Chile in 1959 and Austria in 1961, where he attended the Second Vatican Council. Pope Paul VI elevated him to the College of Cardinals on 24 May 1976 and named him president of the Pontifical Council for the Laity the following month; he participated in the two conclaves that elected John Paul I and John Paul II. He served as cardinal protodeacon from 1983 until 1987, when he opted for the order of cardinal priests, and he remained a prominent figure in the Church until his death in Rome on 9 February 2004.

curiosities.text: He was born in New York but spent his formative years in Italy.
He served as a Vatican diplomat in several European countries during World War II, including Germany and the Netherlands.
He was the longest‑serving Cardinal‑Deacon before being promoted to cardinal priest, holding the title from 1983 to 1987.
